newsitem.title: GERMANY: Continental brings German cargo sales in-house.
newsitem.headline: Continental brings German cargo sales in-house.

text.p: Continental Airlines said it has set up an in-house cargo sales team for Germany in place of the previous general sales agent.
Andreas Gutberlet, the new cargo sales manager Germany, said a four-person sales unit had been in operation at Frankfurt airport since May 1.
Continental Airlines airfreight capacity was previously sold in Germany by Air Canada acting as a GSA, he told Reuters in an interview.
"Continental now believes much more strongly in the significance of air cargo and expansion of cargo revenue through its own staff," he stated.
In-house sales would allow the airline to improve quality by reacting more quickly to customer needs and ensuring basic services were correctly carried out, he said.

Gutberlet said Continental would gain an extra 12-15 tonnes of daily freight capacity with the addition of a second daily Frankfurt-Newark DC10-30 flight which will operate from July 1 until August 31 for the summer holiday season.
The airline now flies daily from Duesseldorf and Frankfurt to New York's Newark airport with DC10-30 aircraft.
Continental carried an average of 1,100 tonnes a month between Germany and the U.S., with 600 tonnes of German export freight and 500 tonnes of U.S. export freight, he said.
The airline averaged ten tonnes of freight per flight on the maximum available DC10-30 capacity of 15 tonnes.
"The load factor is not too bad but of course I want to increase it," Gutberlet said.
